what_its_for: Crofelemer is used to relieve non-infectious diarrhea (diarrhea not caused by an infection) in adults who are taking HIV/AIDS medicines. It helps reduce the number of loose or watery stools you have each day.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablet. If you have trouble swallowing it whole, talk to your doctor or pharmacist about other options.
dosing: The usual dose is one 125 mg tablet taken by mouth twice a day — once in the morning and once in the evening. Try to take it at the same times each day to help you remember.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store crofelemer at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep this medicine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children and pets. Do not store it in the bathroom.
what_to_avoid: There are no specific foods or drinks known to interact with crofelemer, but talk to your doctor or pharmacist before starting any new prescription medicines, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or herbal supplements. Let your care team know about everything you are taking.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if your diarrhea gets worse or does not improve, if you develop signs of dehydration (such as extreme thirst, dry mouth, dark urine, dizziness, or not urinating), if you have blood in your stool, if you develop a fever, or if you experience severe stomach pain or cramping. Also call if you notice any new or unusual symptoms after starting this medicine.
when_it_works: Some people start to see improvement in their diarrhea within the first few days to weeks of starting crofelemer. However, it may take up to 4 weeks to notice the full benefit. Keep taking it as directed even if you do not see immediate improvement, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before taking crofelemer, as the safety of this medicine in pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully studied. Crofelemer is not approved for use in children. If you have liver or kidney problems, let your doctor know, although dose adjustments are generally not required.
